title: RW Aurigae
blurb: A young star with unsteady light: about 60% brighter a year later.
story: RW Aurigae is a young star still pulling in gas from the disc around it, and its light is famously unsteady. Between September 2025 and September 2026 SPHEREx saw it grow about 60% brighter at these wavelengths, while the stars around it stayed the same. Blink the first and last visit, then open its doodle to see the brightness at each visit.

spectrum.hint: The measurements scatter too much to read a pattern. That happens when an object is so bright that it overloads the detector, or when it is changing while SPHEREx watches. Each point is a separate exposure, taken at a different time. This object also changes with time, so colour and change are mixed here.

doodles.explain: It stays in the same place but brightened by about 59% between visits, after allowing for the different infrared colour of each exposure. Stars that pulse, flare or get eclipsed do this. This is V* RW Aur, a known young variable star (SIMBAD).

source: NASA/IPAC IRSA SPHEREx Level-2 spectral images (collections spherex_dr1, spherex_qr3)
